skipped.saturn: No global cylindrical colour map of Saturn's cloud tops is published on NASA / JPL / USGS domains; Cassini maps there cover only the moons and rings.
skipped.uranus: Voyager 2 saw an almost featureless disc; no global map exists from NASA sources.
skipped.neptune: Voyager 2 imaged only part of the planet during one flyby; no global map exists from NASA sources.

mercury.credit: NASA / Johns Hopkins APL / Carnegie Institution of Washington; MESSENGER MDIS stereo-control DEM v2 by USGS Astrogeology (Becker et al. 2016)
mercury.licence: Public domain (NASA mission data, distributed by USGS)
mercury.projection: simple cylindrical (equirectangular), latitude +90 at the top edge, -90 at the bottom
mercury.resampling: area average of every source cell; minMetres / maxMetres are the extremes of this 1024x512 average, not of the source
mercury.notes: Source 23040x11520 (64 px/deg, 665 m/px), int16 x 0.5 m; the file spans 0..360 E (centre 180), rolled so -180 is at the left. Interpolated from a stereo control-network point cloud and smoothed, so craters are softened. No gaps after averaging. Lowest cell is Rachmaninoff basin, highest is south of the equator near 61 E.

venus.credit: NASA / JPL / MIT; Magellan radar altimetry (GTDR), mosaic by USGS Astrogeology
venus.licence: Public domain (NASA mission data, distributed by USGS)
venus.projection: simple cylindrical (equirectangular), latitude +90 at the top edge, -90 at the bottom
venus.resampling: area average of every source cell; minMetres / maxMetres are the extremes of this 1024x512 average, not of the source
venus.notes: Source 8192x4096 (4641 m/px) resampled from the Magellan GTDR altimetry, whose true footprint is 10-30 km, so fine detail is interpolated. 8.3 % of source cells have no altimetry: the caps within about 2 deg of each pole and swaths at 60-80 S and near 80 N. Output cells with no data at all (7.6 %) are filled with the mean of their neighbours, growing inward, so those areas are smooth guesses, not measurements.

earth.credit: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information; ETOPO1 Global Relief Model, ice surface (Amante & Eakins 2009)
earth.licence: Public domain (US Government work, NOAA NCEI)
earth.projection: simple cylindrical (equirectangular), latitude +90 at the top edge, -90 at the bottom
earth.resampling: area average of every source cell; minMetres / maxMetres are the extremes of this 1024x512 average, not of the source
earth.notes: Source 21600x10800 (1 arc-minute) int16 metres, cell registered; land topography and ocean bathymetry in one grid, top of the Antarctic and Greenland ice sheets. No gaps. Area averaging over about 39 km cells flattens the tallest peaks and deepest trenches, so the range (Tibet to the Mariana Trench) is smaller than Everest to Challenger Deep.
